newsitem.title: POLAND: PAY DISPUTE NEARS END AT POLISH KGHM COPPER FIRM.
newsitem.headline: PAY DISPUTE NEARS END AT POLISH KGHM COPPER FIRM.

text.p: A dispute over wage increases at Poland's KGHM copper combine has neared an end as one of the two powerful unions has accepted pay rises proposed by management, PAP news agency reported on Tuesday.

PAP said the Union of Copper Industry Workers (ZZPPM) on Monday officially ended a collective labour dispute with management after it offered workers a five-percent wage rise as of 1997 and a one-off average bonus of 300 zlotys in December.

KGHM, one of the world's largest copper and silver producers, is slated for privatisation in the second quarter of 1997. The value of the concern, employing a total of 42,500, is estimated at $2-3 billion.
The ZZPPM union had demanded a nearly six-percent increase of the average salary, now at 2,000 zlotys and high compared to earnings at other enterprises.

Solidarity -- the second largest union at the plant and which has not yet ended its dispute -- has demanded a monthly rise of 150 zlotys, or 7.5 percent of the average pay of the company's 27,000 workers employed directly in production.

Solidarity also opposes the restructuring of the firm, under which a part of the workforce employed directly in production would be moved to KGHM's fully owned auxiliary firms or subsidiaries involved in services.
PAP, which provided no sources in its report, said that talks on restructuring would continue later in December.
KGHM's spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
